pr_title: dhcp-server: save bound leases to persistent storage, and load it on start
pr_comments: Finally, it is ready for review. PTAL!
so looks good in general, i just would like some care taken that we work sensibly in an environment with /var/ being still absent.

i do wonder how useful this is going to be IRL, i.e. given that we are an early boot service, possibly already running in the initrd, where we can't really load the lease, even if we wanted... I am not against adding this though, since it sounds useful for interfaces triggered later though.

so, to be fully correct we would have to tell networkd when /var/ is around, similar to how we do it for journald. And then later, tell it when /var/ is gone again.

And then, when networkd is told about /var/ being ready it would have to reread all leases...

I have the suspicion that it would be nicest of networkd would keep a primary set of leases under /run/, and only treat the stuff in /var/ as a secondary copy of it. So that people would inotify watch the version in /run, not the one in /var.

> And then, when networkd is told about /var/ being ready it would have to reread all leases...

I don't think that'd be useful. If networkd is told to configure an interface, by the time we have mounted `/var`, it'll most likely have already reacquired the lease. I see two possibilities: for some interfaces, we mark the interface as "requiring /var" and let networkd delay the configuration of that interface. Yu rewrote the networkd internals to allow asynchronous operation, so this actually might be feasible to implement cleanly. A different approach would be to push the storage for certain leases to e.g. an EFI variable, so that it becomes available very early in boot. But I'm not sure if that's worth the trouble.

@poettering @keszybz Thank you for the review.
In the revised version, a minimal subset of that @poettering requested is implemented. Please take a look!

I'll add that to my TODO list.

hmm, i am a bit concerned about making this a per-interface thing and a per-dhcp thing. I don't see the point of making it so fine grained. After all we really just care about two global states: before /var/ is mounted, and after /var/ is mounted. starting individual dhcp servers on individual interfaces sounds needlessly complex to me.

the way i though this would work is if there'd be a new boolean field in struct `Manager` called `persistent_storage_ready` or so. And the service would just toggle that bool via varlink, once during boot and once during shutdown. And all dhcp servers would react to this simultaneously the same way.

and the nice thing would be that this is generic, so if we one day we have other resources we need to persist (for example, it might make sense to also save acquired leases to disk in some scenarios, in the dhcp client, or any other info in fact that takes time to acquire and that would make sense to keep around for quick turnarounds, outside of the realm of dhcp) we have a generic knob already for that.

That should be happens when the server change to use the address range, e.g. previously 192.168.0.0/24 but now 192.168.1.0/24. Even in such case, as already said, I intentionally keep the previous leases in 192.168.0.0/24, as the address range change may be misconfiguration, and the server may soon restarted again with the previous range.

I'd like to merge the PR as is, and will submit follow-up commit to improve the situation of running DHCP server with Address=0.0.0.0/24 in container.

issue_context.title: The "Describe" method starts failing when the DHCP server receives messages with non UTF-8 hostnames
issue_context.body:
When the DHCP server receives DHCPDISCOVER messages with non UTF-8 hostnames like
```python
>>> rdpcap('dhcp-non-utf-8-hostname.pcap')[0][DHCP].options
[('message-type', 1),
 ('client_id', b'\xffX\x88\xc0\xc1\x00\x02\x00\x00\xab\x11o;\xa9\x08 p\xa5S'),
 ('param_req_list', [1, 3, 6, 12, 15, 33, 42, 101, 114, 120, 121]),
 ('max_dhcp_size', 1472),
 ('rapid_commit', b''),
 ('hostname', b'\xff\xfe'),
 'end']
```
the "Describe" method starts failing with "Structure needs cleaning":
```sh
networkctl status  --json short 
Failed to get description: Structure needs cleaning

busctl call org.freedesktop.network1 /org/freedesktop/network1 org.freedesktop.network1.Manager Describe
Call failed: Structure needs cleaning
```
```sh
varlink-25: Changing state processing-disconnect → disconnected
Got message type=method_call sender=:1.16354 destination=org.freedesktop.network1 path=/org/freedesktop/network1 interface=org.freedesktop.network1.Manager member=Describe  cookie=2 reply_cookie=0 signature=n/a error-name=n/a error-message=n/a
Failed to build JSON data: Structure needs cleaning
Sent message type=error sender=n/a destination=:1.16354 path=n/a interface=n/a member=n/a cookie=41 reply_cookie=2 signature=s error-name=System.Error.EUCLEAN error-message=Structure needs cleaning
Failed to process message type=method_call sender=:1.16354 destination=org.freedesktop.network1 path=/org/freedesktop/network1 interface=org.freedesktop.network1.Manager member=Describe cookie=2 reply_cookie=0 signature=n/a error-name=n/a error-message=n/a: Structure needs cleaning
```
It was found in https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/30021#discussion_r1518478633 and should be partly addressed in that PR but I'm not sure why UTF-8 should be enforced there in the first place.
comments:
I am pretty sure we should enforce UTF-8 everywhere, and ever pass that on. I see no reason why we would allow this through for consumption of apps further up the stack. I mean, we are too dumb to handle this correctly right now, and when we fix this, then I am sure similar issues arise on every other level of the stack too, which will mishandle this.

If there was a valid usecase for non-UTF8 hostnames it might be something to cover, but I see none, hence I'd just suppress or escape the bad data, and not let it leak to higher levels of the stack.

Turns out valid UTF-8 isn't always handled well either: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/30021#discussion_r1519212098

I agree that random stuff should't be supplied to the consumers of this API. What I was looking for probably is `HostnameRaw` with raw bytes instead of just `null`s.

Having experimented with this PR I think it would be great to make it easier to clean up leases. Previously to get rid of nonsensical leases it was possible to just restart networkd. With this PR applied networkd has to be stopped and the`/var/lib/systemd/network/dhcp-server-lease/*` files have to be removed manually as far as I can tell.

Also based on my experiments networkd doesn't react to DHCP packets at all until the storage is ready. I'm not sure it's necessary when the DHCP server just relays packets. I'm not sure it should stop handing out leases with no storage either. My understanding is that the idea was to hand out leases (regardless of whether the storage is ready or not) and then save it once the "persistent storage" is ready. Dunno. I haven't fully read the thread yet.

>  I'm not sure it's necessary when the DHCP server just relays packets.

Good point! Yeah, it is not necessary to wait for the persistent storage when the server is running in relay mode. Fixed.

> I'm not sure it should stop handing out leases with no storage either. My understanding is that the idea was to hand out leases (regardless of whether the storage is ready or not) and then save it once the "persistent storage" is ready. Dunno. I haven't fully read the thread yet.

If /var/lib/systemd/network is on a non-root partition, then we need to wait the partition is mounted. Otherwise, on reboot, the DHCP server may start before the partition is mounted, hence we cannot load previously bound leases, and an address already assigned to a host may be bound to another host.
So, we need to read the lease file before starting the DHCP server, and to support that we need to wait for the persistent storage being ready.

> Having experimented with this PR I think it would be great to make it easier to clean up leases. Previously to get rid of nonsensical leases it was possible to just restart networkd. With this PR applied networkd has to be stopped and the`/var/lib/systemd/network/dhcp-server-lease/*` files have to be removed manually as far as I can tell.

Right. So, I also updated the our test script, to remove the persistent storage before starting networkd cleanly.

Interesting. But that's intended. Any leases should be dropped only when it is expired.
BTW, when picking up an IPv4 address requested with a null address, e.g. 0.0.0.0/24, I think we should take into account the lease file.

I believe the lifetime is `DHCP_MAX_LEASE_TIME_USEC` there so they aren't going to expire any time soon :-) Admittedly this particular scenario where one container consumes all the leases, never sends DHCPRELEASE messages back and then gets rebooted isn't normal but at least it should probably be documented how to start networkd with a clean slate or something like that.
